Definition: of Latin origin; apparently "popular"; Poplius (i.e. Publius), a Roman:--Publius.
BiblicalUsage: Publius is the chief man of Malta, and Luke tells his story in two verses. He receives Paul and his companions courteously for three days, and Paul heals his father, who lay sick of a fever and a bloody flux. The whole island watches, and many others come to be healed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe kindness to strangers opens doors the gospel walks through, and Publius shows it plainly. He lodged Paul, and Paul's God healed his father.
